variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense substitution, p.(Glu332Ter) (from the batch HGVS). Both papers describe the disease mechanism as loss of function.

quotes.quote: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a severe childhood-onset inflammatory disease characterized by heterozygous germline loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in TNFAIP3 (1, 2).
Loss-of-function mutation in TNFAIP3 will trigger a new autoinflammatory disease: HA20.

concerns: 34011076 writes the protein as 'p.Glu332' without a stop symbol; the batch protein_check reports agreement with p.(Glu332Ter).

34011076 is a case report whose Table 1 summarises earlier literature; this variant appears there only as a review row citing Aeschlimann et al. (ref 16, a reply letter), with no case description in this paper.

Carrier possibly missing from the batch: 34011076 Table 1 row 29 ('|  |  | 6 mo | F |', Family 13) sits under the c.994G>T family row with a blank variant cell, following the table's convention for relatives; it is not in this batch.

Possible overlap: 39167656 includes NIH-affiliated authors and a cohort of published HA20 families; whether its Family-6 is the Aeschlimann family cited in 34011076 cannot be determined (39167656 gives no sex or age for HA20-32).

39167656 contradicts itself on which patient was single-cell sequenced: the Fig. 6C legend names HA20-34 (6237 cells), while the Results and Methods name HA20-21 (1454 + 6237 = 7691 cells). Any single-cell data attributed to HA20-34 should be treated with caution.
No transcript stated in either paper; the batch uses NM_001270508.2.
notes_for_panel: Evidence is limited to table entries: a review row in 34011076 and a family listing in 39167656. No functional, population or in-silico data.
